input.prompt: The planner prices every Slice at roughly Opus prices because it takes the median over all past Slices, whatever model they ran on, so a Haiku Slice gets a cost way too high. Can you make a Slice's predicted cost come from past Slices run on its own model and effort?

required: a Slice's prediction: the median of the first pool with three measured Slices, corrected by the geometric mean of actual over predicted, pulled toward none (P16)
slice start records the prediction beside the first reading, and slice close keeps it beside the actual
a Slice's cost comes from Slices run on its model and effort once three are measured, else from all, naming the model most of it was measured on; context and time from all (P8 of A-005)
a prediction whose cost was measured on another model than its Slice ran on corrects its context and time, not later costs
slice start and estimate --plan price by the model and effort of the transcript's newest request
estimate --plan lays the Slices left across compaction cycles, with the totals, the oversized and the parallel
estimate --plan before three Slices are measured anywhere: this compaction cycle's rate, from --done
Slices measured with --used carry context only: the prediction and the plan give no time or cost for them
estimate --project and --store add up what was measured, and size a task with nothing measured from others' data
a sized Slice: its files times the median per-file rate, corrected only by sized predictions, and a zero reading is not measured (P13 to P18)
slice start writes Size and Base, slice close writes Files from Base to HEAD, and slice size adds Files to an older Slice
